name: Mohd Nassuruddin Daud
_note: M2 opposition-executive cohort: Menteri Besar of Kelantan, sworn 15 Aug 2023. Added to populate the sub-national-executive class with opposition (PN) executives for the partisan-signal comparison. Objective spine (A5) plus Layer B editorial evidence on file; NO coder panel yet, so Layer B is unscored and the leader is below ranking validity. Layer B carries anchor values pending an independent coder panel (methodology.validity.minCodersToScore=3). Citations verified to exist via search; article full text was not opened (environment fetch restriction); facts rest on cross-outlet-corroborated search summaries and require primary-source reconfirmation. A5 is a negative finding (no personal court/MACC matter located), not a positive clearance. B4 and B5 carry no qualifying event and are left unscored.

metrics.justification: No personal corruption charge, MACC charge, or open investigation naming Mohd Nassuruddin as a subject was located across named outlets as of this record. Malaysian law does not mandate asset declaration to MACC, so the absence of a public declaration is not itself an integrity finding. Recorded as the subject's own status: none on record (an absence-of-evidence finding, scored identically to declared/acquitted).

During the late-November to December 2024 monsoon floods, Kelantan was the hardest-hit state (about 93,763 people in relief centres by 1 Dec 2024); he distributed aid personally, navigating floodwaters by boat in November 2024, while the state relied on federal NADMA tent deployments after local relief-centre supplies ran short. Documented hands-on response managed substantially through a federal backstop (anchor 2).

citation.title: Kelantan MB pilots boat to distribute donations to flood victims

metrics.justification: On clean-water access, a problem unresolved for over 25 years with roughly half the state's population still dependent on wells, his administration stated in November 2024 that the issue is expected to be resolved only by 2028 (target of 58 treatment plants and extensive pipe replacement). A long-promised reform still undelivered within the tenure, with the target deferred (anchor 1).

citation.title: Kelantan expects its water woes to be over by 2028

metrics.justification: Despite the PN-PH federal divide, he publicly thanked PM Anwar Ibrahim and pledged to work with Putrajaya on water and flood mitigation (2024), acknowledging federal allocations for state infrastructure; relations with state opposition assemblymen over development allocations were meanwhile strained. Worked across coalition lines on service delivery without documented institutional strengthening (anchor 2).

citation.title: Water woes: Kelantan MB thanks PM, ready to work with Putrajaya
